_comment: Dashboard settings that shape the page's layout. `npm run build` builds them into its CSS, since a layout value arriving from the server after the first paint would make the page jump. An operator's copy in app-config/user-configurable/ takes effect at the next build. The dashboard's other settings: ui-defaults_non-layout_for-server-up-scenario.json, which the server sends, and ui-defaults_non-layout_for-server-down-scenario.json, built into the page for while the server is unreachable.
_dialogMaxHeightPx_comment: Maximum height, in pixels, of EVERY dashboard dialog: both families (.modal in style.css and .9mm-pos-mgr-modal in 9mm-pos-mgr.css, with their variants) and the IL/G debug popover. Past it a dialog scrolls instead of growing until its dismiss button is pushed off-screen. A dialog with a .9mm-pos-mgr-modal-body scrolls just that body, keeping title and Close button pinned; the rest scroll whole, hence the box's overflow-y. DELIBERATELY EXEMPT: the Disclosure (.disclaimer-box), whose accept/decline buttons the user must scroll the whole text to reach. Anchored dropdowns (the Settings gear's menu, hover info popovers) are not dialogs. scripts/build-ui-tokens.js writes it into the generated src/client/web/ui-tokens.css as --dialog-max-h, so it applies on first paint with no inline style or runtime fetch. The literal lives here only: the CSS uses the variable with no fallback, so without the generated file the dialogs grow and the overlay scrolls.
